The 2025 Million LLMs track reframed retrieval: instead of ranking documents,
systems ranked model IDs by how likely each simulated expert was to answer a new
question well. The pool contained 1,131 cluster-backed expert IDs. Participants
could use released historical queries, precomputed answers, and response
metadata, but they could not call the candidates on a test question. That makes
the prior track a close methodological predecessor to 2026, not a study of
interchangeable commercial foundation models.

## What the official results support

The strongest systems combined several kinds of historical evidence. SRCB's
`submission_4` led the official nDCG@10 ranking with a pipeline built around
weak labels and Qwen3-Embedding-8B representations. UDInfo combined judged
neighbors, global candidate priors, and query-domain clusters. GenAIus showed
that classical expert search remained competitive: retrieve individual past
responses with BM25/RM3, then aggregate their scores back to the candidate that
produced them. Across papers, response-level evidence was generally more useful
than one giant profile per candidate, while embeddings, log-probability
summaries, and learned rankers were most credible when paired with meaningful
behavioral evidence.

These findings define useful 2026 controls: stable priors, sparse and dense
query retrieval, response retrieval, normalized evidence aggregation, and
auditable weak-label features. They do not establish which combination wins on
the new candidate pool.

## Evaluation and comparability boundary

The official overview reports 50 test questions, ground-truth answers for 37,
and only 16 questions with at least one relevant candidate answer. Final labels
used GPT-5-as-judge after the planned pooled human assessment was not completed.
The leaderboard is therefore a valuable first method comparison, but small
differences are fragile. Its scores are neither hidden-test evidence for 2026
nor proof that a method transfers across a changed candidate pool, discovery
set, and judgment process. All local claims in this hub remain development
claims until the organizer's hidden evaluation.
